output.summary: The request (SH-CS, claim CL-01) was to build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and auto-fixes whatever causes wrong bills, triggered by dispute tickets roughly doubling from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month since August (E-02). Investigation ruled out slow ticket handling (E-03, within SLA) and a tariff change (E-04). An initial problem framing (PD-1@v1) blaming field route-completion shortfalls (E-05, E-07) for part of the surge was invalidated once vendor MDMS access was provisioned and queried (E-12): all 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills sit on AMI accounts, with 1184 (95.5%) having valid pre-cutoff AMI reads that were wrongly rejected at billing import as HIGH_CONSUMPTION. This traces to validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), comparing raw register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none', while firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units (E-14) - causing legitimate high-usage reads to look ~10x inflated. This mechanism is corroborated by three independent queries (E-15, E-16, E-17). The successor problem (PD-1@v2) was defined on this basis and passed its DEFINE gate CONDITIONAL_PASS. The release delivers this diagnostic finding plus analysis of the AMI/billing data (per SD-2's release scope), and the original auto-answer/auto-fix request is effectively descoped since response time is not the bottleneck and automated bill writes are prohibited outright (constraint K-BILLWRITE). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no holds): the diagnostic deliverable is complete and actionable, but several follow-on items (the larger ACTUAL-read dispute cohort's cause, the production-readiness of a BV-17 fix, and the actual bill correction) remain open and are tracked as verification obligations/unknowns rather than blocking release outright.
key_points: Trigger: dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026), per E-02; SH-CS's original request (CL-01) was to build an auto-answer/auto-fix AI agent.
Ruled out as causes: slow dispute response (median 1.6d/p90 2.8d within 3.0d SLA, E-03) and tariff changes (none logged, E-04).

The original hypothesis that field route-completion shortfalls (E-05) and reader staffing shortage (E-07, SH-FIELD claim) caused the ESTIMATED-read disputes was invalidated by E-12, since that cohort sits entirely on AMI accounts, not manual-read accounts.

Confirmed root cause for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills: billing rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) applies unit_scaling='none', mismatching firmware v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 register units (E-14), causing 1184 valid high-usage AMI reads to be wrongly rejected (E-12), corroborated independently by E-15, E-16, E-17.

The majority disputed-bill cohort (1785 of 3025, built from ACTUAL reads, E-01) has an unknown root cause; this is tracked as open unknown U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE / VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE and the queries needed to resolve it (DA-RULES, DA-TICKET) are outside this release's scope.

The original auto-answer/auto-fix agent request was effectively descoped: automated bill writes are categorically prohibited by constraint K-BILLWRITE (requires Billing Operations approval), and no write/protected_action exists on the billing-config tool surface to deploy a BV-17 fix this cycle.

Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, no holds. The DEFINE gate for the successor problem passed as CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than blocking the whole release.
limitations_explained: The successor problem's DEFINE gate was a CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some investigative items were deferred rather than fully resolved before proceeding; those deferrals are now tracked as open verification obligations (VOBs).

The cause of the larger ACTUAL-read disputed-bill cohort (1785 of 3025, ~59% of disputes, E-01) is still unknown; VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE is open and the queries needed to investigate it (billing rule log DA-RULES, ticket pattern analysis DA-TICKET) fall outside this release's scope.

Before any production fix to BV-17's unit-scaling handling, it remains unresolved (VOB-R-4, open) whether correcting it could reintroduce a risk of missing genuinely anomalous high-consumption reads, such as leaks or tampering.

The success criterion that the ACTUAL-read share of disputes drops substantially from its current ~59% (M-DISPUTED-BILLS-ACTUAL-SHARE) has not been met and depends on resolving the still-unknown ACTUAL-read cohort cause.

Whether the monthly CRM dispute-ticket count validly proxies the rate of actually-incorrect bills (as opposed to counting unrelated or duplicate tickets) remains unconfirmed; this assumption is still open (U-DISPUTE-METRIC-VALIDITY).

A structural fix to billing rule BV-17 cannot be deployed this cycle because the billing-config tool surface is read-only in this release, with no write or protected action defined for making the fix.
The completeness of the MDMS AMI read-event data behind the ESTIMATED-read cohort is unknown (A-MDMS-COMPLETENESS), so the extent of AMI-side confirmation coverage for that cohort is uncertain.

No automated capability exists to write bill corrections; the manual rebate for the 1184 confirmed wrongly-rejected accounts must be carried out by Billing Operations under the K-BILLWRITE approval requirement, not by this release's agent.
